content:
If I could make one change to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I'd choose to disable the new gesture of swiping down from the top of the screen to summon Siri AI. There are already many other ways to invoke Siri, so there's no need to ruin a gesture I've become accustomed to using to open Notification Center.

Meanwhile, on the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even though it's already late August, the new beta versions are still adding welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's still one change I'm hoping to see.

Battery percentage is harder to read on MacBooks running macOS 27 Golden Gate

macOS 27 Golden Gate has redesigned the battery controls in the menu bar. By default, the percentage is not displayed — only a battery-shaped visual icon.

It actually looks quite nice. I keep the percentage turned off on my iPhone and use the same battery icon. But I've always liked seeing the percentage on my Mac.

If you enable the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number is placed inside the battery icon. I'm guessing this is to keep it consistent with the approach used for iPhone in iOS 27.

Cramming the percentage inside the battery icon is Apple's solution for making the most of the space in the top-right corner of the iPhone screen (whether next to the notch or the Dynamic Island). But on the Mac, I don't see a real placement issue, even in the menu bar.

Since the first developer beta was released, I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on my 15-inch MacBook Air. I've noticed that my overall attention to the battery percentage has dropped, because for me the number is no longer as clear and easy to read as before.

I hope Apple will reconsider this design decision in the future, especially if other users feel the same way. During this transition period, I've at least solved the problem for myself.

I used Codex to build a simple menu bar utility that clearly displays battery status and percentage, achieving exactly the effect I wanted. If you think you might need it too, you can download and install it for free here.
